writeup.headline: Gold Fields rates Hold: solid revenue growth and decent quality offset by a weak share-price trend and Ghana lease risk.
writeup.thesis: Gold Fields scores 55, a Hold, with valuation left out because the inputs for this foreign filer could not be reconciled. Growth is the strongest factor at 82, with TTM revenue growth of 15.6% and growth sped up by 10.6 pp from the previous quarter. Quality scores 65 on a 45.3% gross margin, an 8.1% FCF margin and almost no dilution (diluted share count up 0.1% year on year). The balance sheet is middling at 40, with net debt at 3.86 times free cash flow and cash covering 0.34 of debt. The trend factor drags hardest at 19: the price is 15.4% below its 200-day average, 41.1% below its 52-week high, and the shares are 19.8 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days.
key_risks: Ghana is weighing local takeovers of big mines while it decides on the Tarkwa lease renewal, a material risk to a key asset.
Underground development at Windfall in Quebec was paused after a permit lapsed, adding project and cost risk.
Weak price trend: shares 11.2% below the 50-day average and 41.1% below the 52-week high.
Leverage is meaningful, with net debt at 3.86 times free cash flow and cash covering only 0.34 of debt.
Results depend heavily on the gold price, which could reverse the recent revenue growth.
what_would_change: Up to Buy needs 10 more points, most plausibly from a recovery in the share-price trend (score 19) or a favourable Tarkwa lease outcome lifting news risk.
Down to Sell would take an 11-point drop, for example an adverse Ghana decision, a further slide in the trend factor, or growth fading from 15.6%.
Lower net debt relative to free cash flow would strengthen the balance sheet score from 40.
A usable valuation reading, once price and share count are reconciled, could push the score either way.
